simple.meaning: עֹרֶף (ʻôreph) is a Hebrew action word meaning “the nape or back of the neck (as declining ); hence, the back generally (whether literal or figurative).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 33 times in Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Deuteronomy, Joshua, and 9 more, beginning at Genesis 49:8. The surrounding contexts include family, land, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עֹרֶף (H6203) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: עֹרֶף (ʻôreph) / H6203 is traced through Genesis 49:8, Exodus 23:27, Exodus 32:9, Exodus 33:3 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H6203. oreph עֹ֫רֶף noun masculine Deut 31:27 back of neck, neck ; — ׳ע absolute Josh 7:12 +; construct Gen 49:8 +; suffix עָרְמִּי Job 16:12 , עָרְמְּךָ Deut 31:27 , etc.; — 1 back of neck of fleeing foe בְּע ׳יָָֽדְךָ ׳וגו Gen 49:8 (poem in J), compare בְּעָרְמִּי וְאָחַז Job 16:12 (figurative); Exod 23:27 (E), Psa 18:41 = 2Sam 22:41 ; turn ( מָּנָה הָפַח, ) one's back before ( לִפְנֵי ) a foe Josh 7:8 , 12 (JE), absolute Jer 48:39 ; figurative of apostasy ע ׳מָּנָה אֶל 2:27 ; 32:33 (opposed to פָנִים מָּנָה ) absolute ע ׳וַיִּתְּנּוּ 2Chr 29:6 ; of ׳י s disfavour ׳ע אֶרְאֵם פָנִים וְלֹא Jer 18:17 with the back and not the face will I look at them. 2 figurative in ׳קְשֵׁהעֿ stiff of neck , i.e. obstinate , of Israel Exod 32:8 ; 33:3 , 5 ; 34:9 (all J E), Deut 9:6 , 13 ; הַקָּשֶׁה עָרְמְּךָ 31:27 ; with verb ע ׳הִקְשָׁה i.e. be obstinate, intractable 10:16 ; Jer 7:26 ; 17:23 ; 19:15 ; 2Kin 17:14 (twice in verse); Neh 9:16-17 , 29 ; 2Chr 30:8 ; compare ע בַּרְזֶל ׳גִּיד Isa 48:4 (|| אָ֑תָּה קָשֶׁה ); ע ׳הִקְשָׁה of individual 2Chr 36:13 ; Prov 29:1 . 3 of bird: nip its head עָרְמּוֺ מִמּוּל Lev 5:8 (P).
